incidents.victim: ConnectWise ScreenConnect customers (MSPs and managed endpoints)
incidents.vector: A threat actor exploited an authentication flaw in a ScreenConnect RMM+ extension (an unconfigured, empty access key) to issue remote commands and install an unauthorized client that deployed the SCKit worm.
incidents.impact: SCKit established rogue remote-access channels on MSP-managed endpoints and used a component called RelayTrap to target connecting IT technicians; ConnectWise is investigating roughly 400 compromised customer and partner environments.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 tenants downstream of ConnectWise (2,250+ organizations)
incidents.vector: After compromising ConnectWise application credentials, the group tracked as Storm-0940 used the ARTEX AI-driven penetration-testing framework to accelerate automated sign-in attempts against thousands of downstream Microsoft 365 tenants.
incidents.impact: Follow-on activity included abuse of Microsoft Graph, application credentials, and privilege changes across more than 2,250 affected tenants.

incidents.victim: Government ministries, telecom, defense, pharmaceutical, and financial organizations (200+ orgs, 14 countries)
incidents.vector: The actor, tracked as VAPOR PANDA, used the open-source ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to automate reconnaissance, credential spraying, and exploitation at machine speed across hundreds of targets simultaneously.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike confirmed post-compromise activity at nine organizations and additional credential-scanning or password-spraying against at least 12 others; the FBI separately issued a flash alert warning ARTEX is being used to breach government agencies and critical sectors worldwide, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion claimed by the Qilin ransomware-as-a-service affiliate program; initial access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal information of students and employees was stolen; the university's MachForms portal remains offline while the scope of the data theft is assessed.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of War and Defense Industrial Base (historical Gootloader victims)
incidents.vector: Gootloader malware, spread since 2018 via compromised and malicious websites, infected devices and was sold as botnet access to ransomware affiliates.
incidents.impact: A DOJ-led Operation Endgame action dismantled 235 servers and 257 domains tied to Gootloader, StealC, and CastleRAT; at least 44 U.S. ransomware victims traced to Gootloader infections suffered a combined $28.8 million in losses, including attacks on the Department of War and the Defense Industrial Base.

incidents.victim: City of Osaka and ~400 Arara email-service customers (incl. TKC Corporation, Sega)
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised the Arara email distribution service used by TKC Corporation's administrative services platform, then used the access to send malicious emails impersonating financial institutions.
incidents.impact: More than 1 million Osaka resident email addresses were exposed; the underlying Arara breach exposed roughly 77 million email addresses across nearly 400 customers nationwide, part of a broader wave of cyberattacks battering Japanese organizations.

incidents.victim: ActiveCloud, ESTT, and Beget (Belarusian and Russian cloud hosting providers)
incidents.vector: A series of ransomware and destructive wiper attacks against cloud infrastructure management systems at three regional hosting providers within two weeks.
incidents.impact: ActiveCloud's hosting, email, and virtual server platforms were disrupted for days; Beget lost some customer VM backups after hackers wiped data; no confirmed link between the three incidents or a common attacker has been established.

incidents.vector: Hackers stole and decrypted customer environment variables for roughly 100,000 customers (about 1.85% of its customer base), then used the stolen credentials and tokens to run up AI inference costs.
incidents.impact: Attackers incurred approximately $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage charges; Railway is working with AI providers to refund the costs or cover them directly.

incidents.vector: A months-long intrusion into the Qubole data lake platform by the n0n data extortion group; specific technical access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen nearly 1 petabyte of data spanning all Qubole customers; Qubole declined private negotiation before n0n went public with the claim.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: More than 350 sports clubs and communities using the AllUnited app had customer data stolen.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole troves of student information dating back more than a decade.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor manufacturers, defense-policy organizations, and civil society groups (19 organizations)
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers (tracked as CL-STA-1238) paired the open-source Cairn AI agent framework with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models to autonomously plan and execute 25 intrusion operations, exploiting weak or default passwords and application flaws with minimal human supervision.
incidents.impact: Confirmed unauthorized access or data theft at 10 of 19 targeted organizations, including harvested credentials, exposure of more than one million member records at a U.S. teachers' union, creation of persistent admin accounts at a semiconductor company, and modification of a live industry standards-ballot document.

incidents.vector: North Korean operators (publicly known as Sapphire Sleet, BlueNoroff, APT38, and Stardust Chollima) hijack Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack, and Discord accounts to lure targets into fake video calls on typo-squatted Zoom/Teams clones, then use recorded victim webcam footage to impersonate them in follow-on attacks.
incidents.impact: The scheme drained more than $400 million from crypto and Web3 firms over 18 months; the FBI seized infrastructure containing more than 900 secretly recorded victim videos, and DOJ obtained court authorization to seize $1.2 billion of the funds stolen from Binance.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed customer accounts, suspected via abuse of OAuth connections.
incidents.impact: The AI tools marketplace revoked affected OAuth connections and rotated internal secrets as a precaution following the breach.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the agency's website used by financial institutions to submit security assessments.
incidents.impact: Personal data was stolen from South Korea's financial-sector security regulator.

incidents.victim: European supermarket chains and medical facilities (France and 10+ countries)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited default credentials and vulnerable software on internet-exposed refrigeration controllers to remotely force units into defrost mode.
incidents.impact: Roughly 700 French supermarkets lost inventory in an October wave, with a second wave in early November hitting 100+ locations across 10+ additional countries; temperatures were raised as high as 50°C, causing fires in some cases, and medical facility refrigeration was also affected. French authorities publicly attributed the campaign to IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack claimed by the BYOD ransomware gang; initial access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The university says full restoration of normal operations across all systems will take multiple weeks; payroll, payment, admissions, course registration, and public-safety systems are being prioritized while the scope of any data theft is investigated.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed; government IT teams are investigating.
incidents.impact: Poland suspended its ePUAP e-government portal after detecting a cyberattack; the digital affairs minister said evidence points to a foreign adversary.

incidents.victim: Organizations with exposed VPN appliances (U.S. and Europe, Settra ransomware victims)
incidents.vector: The group tracked as TAG-218 exploited a GlobalProtect VPN authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) and other VPN appliance weaknesses to gain access, then deployed the previously undocumented GhostFrame post-exploitation framework against VMware ESXi hosts to harvest credentials and pivot.
incidents.impact: GhostFrame gave attackers hypervisor-level control over victim virtual machines; four victims were subsequently published on the Settra ransomware leak site.

incidents.vector: Business email compromise; township staff were tricked into wiring funds for a land purchase to a fraudulent account.
incidents.impact: The township lost $26 million; the incident occurred in September but was not disclosed publicly until after a committee election in November.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a third-party platform used by the firm.
incidents.impact: One of the world's largest accounting firms (ninth by revenue) is notifying clients that customer data was stolen in a September breach.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians, law enforcement officials, and journalists
incidents.vector: Doxxing campaign; technical access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal information on senior EU officials, including Italy's foreign minister, Europol and Eurojust leadership, and journalists who had investigated Russian influence operations.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed; consistent with Turla's historical use of compromised infrastructure and custom backdoors.
incidents.impact: Romania's intelligence service (SRI) confirmed a Turla intrusion at one government organization in late 2025, corroborating prior ESET reporting.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed equipment left exposed to the internet, triggering a power outage before expanding across the port's IT network.
incidents.impact: Brazil's largest port operated on manual procedures for five days; internet and telephone connectivity have since been restored. The same port authority refused a $26 million ransom demand from the n0n extortion group in a separate October incident.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks customers with internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell PHP remote-code-execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw against internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed active exploitation gaining root access; only about 0.02% of Palo Alto Networks' installed base had internet-facing management interfaces exposed, and each affected customer was individually notified. Customers who had already patched were not affected.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed; discovered when addresses associated with the platform began showing $0 balances.
incidents.impact: India's oldest cryptocurrency exchange suspended operations after more than 81,000 associated wallet addresses were drained; the total amount stolen had not been disclosed nearly a week after the hack.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: More than 72,000 passport scans were stolen from the ministry.

incidents.victim: Li Auto EV owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers took over master user accounts for Li Auto smart EVs, most linked to Chinese eSIMs provided by importers, to lock legitimate owners out of their vehicles.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners were locked out of their cars and extorted to regain control; the actual number of affected vehicles is believed to be higher.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised three Binance developers (one via a trojanized Homebrew download, others via fake job-interview coding assignments) to obtain wallet-signing privileges, then used a sweeper exploiting Ethereum's EIP-7702 smart-account authorization feature to drain hot wallets.
incidents.impact: Approximately $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency was transferred to attacker-controlled addresses before Binance could fully revoke on-chain authorizations; Binance and law enforcement have since frozen or recovered roughly $2.85-2.9 billion, and DOJ obtained court authorization to seize $1.2 billion of the stolen funds. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.
